platform: macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64). Windows measurements NOT taken -- no Windows device available to this session.
build_configuration: Release, built via `npx tauri build` (NOT raw `cargo build --release`).

metric_1_cold_launch_ms.gap: The scorecard's Measurement Environment Freeze defines cold launch as preceded by a reboot or equivalent guaranteed cold-cache state. No reboot/`purge` was possible in this environment, so these are warm-cache launches. Value recorded for transparency; it must be re-measured in a frozen environment before it is entered into the calculator.
metric_1_cold_launch_ms.variance_note: High spread across runs (40-118.00000000000001 ms), consistent with warm-cache launches on a machine doing other work. Another reason this metric must be re-taken in a frozen environment.

metric_2_interaction_latency_ms.method: In-page performance.now() delta from the Task Detail navigation click until every artifact load has settled and the resulting re-render is committed to the DOM.
metric_2_interaction_latency_ms.correction_note: An earlier revision stamped this at first synchronous paint, while Artifact rows were still showing 'loading...' placeholders. That reported ~1 ms and did not match the scorecard's 'fully rendered and interactive' definition. Corrected to wait for artifact settle, which is why the value rose to ~13 ms. It still excludes the final compositor paint, so treat it as a lower bound.

metric_3_idle_memory_mb.method: `ps -o rss=` against the real OS process, sampled 30s after launch with no interaction -- #370's exact procedure.
metric_3_idle_memory_mb.invalid_run_note: One earlier sample read 45.7 MB against ~96 MB for every other run -- an incomplete launch where the webview had not finished coming up. Discarded and re-run per the scorecard's invalid-run rule rather than averaged in.
metric_3_idle_memory_mb.comparability_caveat: This is RSS of the Tauri main process only. WKWebView renders content in separate WebKit helper processes, so this UNDERCOUNTS true footprint -- and it undercounts in a way single-process Avalonia/Uno spikes will not. #381 must not compare these numbers naively; a like-for-like comparison needs whole-process-tree accounting on every candidate.

metric_4_installed_package_size.gap: The scorecard averages the two OSes and requires both noted in raw evidence. Only macOS is measured; the Windows .msi/.exe size is pending.
metric_4_installed_package_size.caveat: Includes the test-only WebDriver bridge (tauri-plugin-wdio + tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver, see src-tauri/Cargo.toml). A real production build would feature-gate these out, so this over-states size relative to a shipping build.

metric_5_filewatch_response_latency_ms.gap: Scorecard requires a 3-run median timestamped from the acceptance recording. Only a single WebDriver-polled wall-clock observation exists (see evidence/filewatch-live-update.json), which proves the pipeline is live but is NOT the metric value. Per the scorecard's Missing-evidence rule this scores 0 unless captured properly before scoring.

metric_6_accessibility_completeness_pct.gap: Requires a live VoiceOver (macOS) and Narrator (Windows) pass scoring correct accessible name + role + state per hit zone, averaged across both OSes. Automating a screen reader is not appropriate; this is a HITL step for TJ, and the Windows half additionally needs a Windows device. See README.

catalog_coverage.drag-reorder a subtask: subtask-reorder.spec.js (via the accessible Alt+Arrow keyboard alternative)
catalog_coverage.trigger a live file-watch update: filewatch-live-update.spec.js (on the locked 'Confirm Tailscale ACL update' fixture task)

metric_8_implementation_complexity_loc.note: The scorecard excludes 'shared Glasswork.Core logic', written with Avalonia/Uno in mind since they reuse the existing C# Core. Tauri has no such reuse path -- its Core is new code this framework required. Both figures are reported so #381 can pick a fair comparison basis rather than one being silently chosen here.

overall_status: INCOMPLETE -- metrics 2, 3 and 7 meet their locked procedure (with metric 3 carrying a cross-framework comparability caveat); metric 8 is measured with an interpretation note; metric 1 does not meet the cold-cache procedure; metric 4 covers one OS; metrics 5 and 6 are not measured. No value here should be entered into the scorecard calculator until those gaps close.
